title: latency_bench / batch=1 inference cost of every cache executor (pi0.5 teacher, ACT, SmolVLA) on RTX 4090 + Xeon E5-2696 v4

content.per_call_samples: n=200/100 (students, GPU), n=30 (teacher GPU), n=10 (teacher CPU); every file carries its raw per-call list

provenance.measured_by: one process per cell, run serially on an otherwise idle RTX 4090; timing contract identical to the production sidecar forward_ms (sidecar_server.py:92-96) for students and to the staged Policy.infer path (policy.py:101-131) for the teacher; cross-checked against exp/rl_router/microbench_cost.py CUDA-event timing (415.45 ms, n=50)
provenance.notes: Synthetic observations (uint8 224x224 dual view + 8-dim state + the real libero_spatial task_0 prompt) with real frozen weights. Latency depends on tensor shapes and graph structure, not on pixel or weight values. A byte-identical sibling copy of these JSONs sits on weilandserver at /home/weiland/bench_latency/results/, alongside the raw run logs.

caveats: The authority path is inside exp/**/data/** and is therefore swallowed by .gitignore line 6: the experiment-side originals never reach version control. The collected copy under analysis/latency_bench/results/ (next caveat) is what a later reader actually gets from git; verify either side before quoting numbers from a working tree you did not produce.

A git-tracked copy of these 15 JSONs lives at exp/data_authority/analysis/latency_bench/results/ (collected under the registry's analysis rules, digests in that task's MANIFEST.json). The authority path above is the experiment-side original the benchmark scripts wrote; the two are byte-identical at collection time.

eager pi0.5 (448.26 ms) is NOT the production figure. Production with cache goes through InferenceInterceptor._get_or_compile_stages (interceptor.py:304-340), which compiles the three stages and downgrades max-autotune to max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. That production build was not measured: its compilation did not finish in 20+ minutes (single-threaded dynamo tracing/lowering, 33 inductor workers idle at 2.5%). It must fall between the default (200.85) and CUDA-Graph (67.48) rows, near the default end.

The fused (one-graph) rows require --no-builtin-compile. openpi compiles sample_actions itself at construction time (pi0_config.py:35 defaults pytorch_compile_mode to max-autotune; pi0_pytorch.py:234), so an unguarded fused run stacks two compilations. A first round measured that way (default 188.28 / CUDA-Graph 72.11 ms) is void and its two JSONs were deleted; do not resurrect those numbers from older chat logs or report drafts.

For fused + CUDA Graph the in-model total_ms is an artefact (1.75 ms): it times graph SUBMISSION only, kernels are still async. Use the synchronized wall (72.04 ms). The 3-stage rows do not have this problem -- policy.py syncs after every stage.

ACT loads exactly one per-task model (task_0), not the 10-model production ensemble. Residency does not affect per-call latency (routing is a dict lookup) but the number is not a memory-footprint figure.

SmolVLA under CUDA Graph needs torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin() per call, otherwise it raises 'accessing tensor output of CUDAGraphs that has been overwritten' (smolvlm_with_expert.py:51). The recorded 60.64 ms is with that guard.
These are isolated model-forward costs. Retrieval, gate, verdict, websocket round trip and client-side env stepping are all excluded; do not read any row as an end-to-end system latency.

Supersedes the latency table in exp/ablation_study/analysis/analysis.md section 6, which was measured while the sidecar shared the GPU with the pi0.5 server: that table is high by 1.5-2.2x on Stage1/teacher/ACT and low by 1.3x on SmolVLA.

provenance.notes says 'every file carries its raw per-call list'. Measured 2026-08-27: only 4 of the 15 do -- act_cpu_xeon (n=100), act_cuda_4090 (n=200), smolvla_cpu_xeon (n=20), smolvla_cuda_4090 (n=100), all of them uncompiled baselines. Every compiled cell and EVERY pi05 file, teacher_pi05_4090 included, carries summary statistics only (the pi05 files are 460-562 bytes). So a consumer needing a dispersion figure for pi0.5 has mean/median/p90/min and nothing else, and must reconstruct an approximate SD from p90-mean under a distributional assumption.

These cells are in-process microbenchmarks of single forward calls: there is no episode and no block structure anywhere in this dataset. It therefore cannot supply a block-level variance, however the consumer aggregates it. exp/dispatch_surface needed exactly that for its cost-bench power simulation and had to measure it elsewhere (exp/dispatch_surface/analysis/block_variance_probe.py, on the gate_threshold_pareto sweep, which does have paired arms over a shared init pool); see logs/dispatch_surface_plan.log.md section 11.
